newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief Annan not going to South Africa on Timor.
newsitem.headline: UN chief Annan not going to South Africa on Timor.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan will not be visiting South Africa to brief President Nelson Mandela on the conflict in Indonesian-ruled East Timor, the United Nations said on Monday.

South African officials said earlier that Annan would arrive in Pretoria on Friday, but U.N. officials said Mandela and Annan might have misunderstood each other during a cellphone conversation that broke up frequently.
"He is definitely not going," U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said, adding that he personally questioned Annan about the trip.

He said the confusion lay in a planned visit by Annan's special representative, Jamsheed Marker, a Pakistani former U.N. ambassador, who is conducting talks at U.N. headquarters between Portuguese and Indonesian officials.
After they are completed, Marker will travel to South Africa to brief Mandela, who has offered to help the United Nations with the long-running dispute.

Indonesia occupied East Timor in 1975 after a civil war erupted following Portugal's withdrawal from its colony. In 1976 Indonesia incorporated the territory as its 27th province but this has never been recognised by the United Nations.
